steps.title: A browser drawer beside your project
steps.body: In the PC app, the browser now slides in at the right, next to the whole project: the tabs and every page narrow to make room, and you drag the divider to share the width. Each project keeps its own tabs. Hide it and bring it back at any time: the pages keep running and never reload.

keys.text: at the end of the project's tabs: show or hide the drawer
share the width; double-click to reset
a new tab in this project

steps.title: Point at the page, or draw on it, for a chat
steps.body: Select an element and write a note on it, or draw over the page (pins, boxes, freehand), each mark with its own note. Then send it to one of the project's chats, or to Cru: as CSS selectors (each element's note, selector and HTML, as text), or as the full screenshot with your marks drawn in. A drawing has no selector, so once you draw, the screenshot is how it goes. The project's chats can use the drawer's tabs too, and Cru can use every project's, pointing at things where you can see them.

keys.text: select elements or draw on the page
the selected elements as text, no picture
the page with your marks and notes

steps.title: Browse on the server's network
steps.body: When the app is on another computer than the server, each tab can use this computer's network or the server's. On the server's, the tab reaches what only the server can: its localhost dev servers and internal hosts, carried over the app's own signed-in connection. A tab on the server's network is marked SRV.

keys.text: This PC or Server, per tab

steps.title: Tabs that go out through homepool
steps.body: A drawer tab can leave through one of your homepool networks, your home line or a friend's, with the PC browser key you make in the drawer. Each network keeps one exit, so its tabs keep one address, and the tab shows which node it goes through and its IP, or plainly that no exit is up. Chats ask you before they use it, and a network this PC is itself a node of is not offered.

keys.text: This PC, Server, or a homepool network
the PC browser key, its networks, the chats you approved

steps.title: One browser, with history you can clear
steps.body: Every tab in every project shares one browser on this computer: sign in to a site once and every tab is signed in, and it stays that way after a restart. The drawer keeps a history, suggested as you type an address, and you can clear the history, cookies and site data, or cached files, for every site or just one.

keys.text: pages you have visited come up

steps.title: Choose where traffic leaves from
steps.body: The new Homepool tab is a shared exit for chats, scripts and containers. Traffic can leave from the server's own connection, which is the default, or through one of your networks: your phone and PC at home, or a friend's line. You put each device in the network it is really on.

keys.text: the tab: networks, nodes, access, requests, activity
a place, and a device in it

steps.title: Nothing leaves without your say
steps.body: Only a key you made or approved can use homepool, and only through the networks you gave it. A chat asks for access through Crundi's tools and waits for you to approve, change or refuse it. Switch a key off or revoke it, and its connections end at once.

keys.text: what chats asked for: approve, change or refuse
every key, its networks, data used, on or off

steps.title: Share a phone's or a PC's connection
steps.body: In the phone app and the PC app, share this device's connection with one switch, and see its status, network, public IP and data used. For a friend's line, add a node and give them its code: the Homepool Node app, or one Docker command, needs no Crundi sign-in.

keys.text: in the app's Homepool screen, or This PC in the tab
a code, a QR and a Docker line for a friend
